name: Cheesy Beef and Broccoli Rice Bowls
intro_html: This is the bowl for when you want something that feels a little lighter but still fills you up. Lean beef and tender broccoli over rice, pulled together with a splash of beef broth and a melt of cheddar. Real vegetables, real protein, and it still lands right around ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost). Your future self, opening the fridge on a busy Tuesday, will thank you.
ingredients_display: 93/7 Ground Beef (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 3.5 cups dry jasmine: ~$0.86. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Fat Free Cheddar, 1 3/4 cups shredded: ~$1.94. Buy 1 8oz bag: $2.25.
Pantry seasonings (garlic powder, onion powder, salt, black pepper): ~$0.37. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $29.01 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.07 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $32.93 across 14 servings, roughly $2.35 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $5.91 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $38.84. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a balanced, veggie-loaded dinner. Frozen broccoli keeps this cheap and fast year round.
shop_smart: Frozen broccoli beats fresh here. It is cheaper, lasts for months, and cooks straight from the bag with no waste.
Buy the beef on sale and freeze. The one rule that quietly lowers the cost of every batch you make.
Broth in a big carton is cheaper per cup than the little cans, and it keeps in the fridge for your next few batches.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, and season it with the garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper. Drain any excess.
Add the broccoli and the beef broth, cover, and steam a few minutes until the broccoli is bright and tender.
Combine the rice, beef, and broccoli in your big pot and stir. Fold in the shredded cheddar.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container. Every bowl lands near {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

recipeIngredient: Fat Free Cheddar, 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Brown the ground beef, season it with garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, and drain any excess.
Add the broccoli and beef broth, cover, and steam until tender.
Combine rice, beef, and broccoli and fold in the cheddar.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.
